title: Jeremy Doku World Cup: 'Not against' journalist after criticism over leaving Belgium camp to attend birth

intro: Belgian winger Jeremy Doku has responded to criticism after revealing he planned to leave the national team camp at the World Cup to be present for the birth of his first child. Speaking to the media, Doku said he was "not against" the journalist who questioned the timing of his decision, according to a report by BBC Sport. This exchange has highlighted the sometimes sensitive intersection between elite tournaments and players' personal lives.

sections.heading: What the BBC Sport report says
sections.text: According to BBC Sport, Jeremy Doku stated he is "not against" the journalist who criticised his intention to depart Belgium's World Cup camp in order to attend the birth of his first child. The core facts reported are limited to Doku's comment and the nature of the criticism — that it concerned his plan to leave the squad during the tournament to be with his partner for the birth. No further claims, quotes or timing details are provided in that excerpt.

sections.heading: Why this matters: balancing national duty and family
sections.text:
Situations in which players must choose between major international duties and significant family events often attract public and media scrutiny. The World Cup is one of the most prominent competitions in global sport, and national team camps are structured to maximise focus and preparation. At the same time, becoming a parent is a major life event and many teams have protocols or make individual arrangements to allow players to be present for childbirth when possible.

Debates around these moments typically involve questions about squad continuity, the manager's plans, and the player's commitments to teammates and fans. Public commentary can be strong, both in support of players prioritising family and from those who feel squad obligations should come first. Doku's measured response — saying he is "not against" the critic — may reflect an attempt to de-escalate tensions and acknowledge the differing perspectives involved.

analysis: This episode underlines the broader conversation about player welfare and media scrutiny at major tournaments. Analysts might see Doku's comment as an attempt to defuse a potentially divisive issue — acknowledging the critic while standing by a personal decision. From a team-management perspective, these cases are often handled behind closed doors through discussion between the player, coaching staff and federation, but public reactions can still influence narratives. Fans and pundits tend to bring strong views, and the way a player responds publicly can shape perceptions long after the event.
